These remain historical controlled/internal-source contributions, not live checkout delivery, production payment verification, current-branch availability, prerequisite-qualified checkout behavior, or automatic discount application.

Newly demonstrated by the latest assessment: the selected prod-derived baseline is no longer wholly uninspected. The committed tree for `auto-50-perc-off` / prod commit `45826e12cdc8f585e514d7bb09c0d37fa28ed568` was assessed at source level. The active worktree was still `feature/kiosk-square-return-recovery`, so this is best treated as inspection of the selected committed tree, not execution from a checked-out delivery branch. Within the inspected customer web path, the assessment found the directed prerequisite storage/reader missing, named historical purchase-evidence services absent, and the automatic 50% selector missing from baseline source. It also identified reusable existing surfaces: recognition/search helpers, purchase-history/payment-related behavior, customer checkout routes, redeem-code cookie preview behavior, and `postPayment` discount persistence before provider handling. Those supplied-code paths establish existing manual/supplied-code discount handling, but they do not establish prerequisite-based qualification or automatic discovery of an applicable 50% code.

The latest research changed the current distance-to-goal picture by reducing branch/source uncertainty and identifying a first supported implementation boundary: restore directed tour-prerequisite storage and reader on the prod-based branch, with checkout tour ID and configured directed tour pairs as inputs, configured status and prerequisite tour IDs as outputs, and acceptance cases for configured tours, multiple prerequisites, unconfigured tours, direction, and isolated rollback. That boundary is decision-enabling research, not implemented product progress; its acceptance cases are proposed checks, not newly passing tests.

The inspected source does not establish the integrated connections for prerequisite lookup, recognition-to-paid-purchase qualification, automatic applicable-code discovery, or automatic qualified discount application before payment.
